entries.effect: one item of the document's /Outlines tree, which PDF 1.7 Table 8.2 makes a LINKED structure: the catalog names a root dictionary through /Outlines, every item names its /Parent, /Prev and /Next, and an item's children are its /First .. /Last chain.  Every member here is read by walking those links with the release's own dictionary and array readers, and the whole tree is reached through -[PDFDocument outlineRoot].  The children are built once and memoised because both -numberOfChildren and -childAtIndex: walk the same chain.  -insertChild:atIndex: and -removeFromParent are NOT implemented and their rows say why

entries.effect: the item at that position, and there are TWO out-of-range answers on the host rather than one, both measured over outline-collapsed.pdf's whole tree with every node asked at every index from 0 to its own child count: a node WITH children RAISES NSRangeException past the end - "childAtIndex: 2 out of bounds" on the root, which has two, and "childAtIndex: 1 out of bounds" on a node with one - and a node with NO children answers NIL, even at index 0.  So the rule is not "past the end raises": a node with a /First chain raises when the index runs off it, and a node with no chain has nothing to walk and answers nil.  The harness compares both through @try, printing the exception's NAME for a raise and nil for the other answer

entries.effect: a positive /Count means OPEN, and the host agrees with PDF 1.7 Table 8.2 on that - an earlier version of this row said the host read the sign the other way round, which was my reading of the specification and not the host's behaviour.  Measured: outline-signs.pdf carries two items of the SAME shape - two children each - one with /Count +4 and one with /Count -4, and the positive one answers YES and the negative one NO.  AND an item with NO /Count answers YES only when it has no /Title either: outline-titlekey.pdf's five leaves differ only in their /Title - absent, an empty /Title (), a real one, absent without /F, absent with a /Dest - and only the absent one answers YES; outline-untitled.pdf and outline-titled.pdf are two chains of four items with the same shape differing only in whether each /Title is written, and the untitled one answers YES at the leaf where the titled one answers NO, three runs out of three.  So: YES when the /Count is positive, and YES when there is no /Count AND no /Title
